Commentary.Commentary: Rashid was the most successful bowler for England while Woakes did extremely well despite not getting a wicket. Stokes was also effective with his reverse swing as the visiting bowlers didn't allow India's batsmen to run away with the game. The lower order contribution from the hosts could be vital, particularly the last wicket stand which added 29. With the track deteriorating, seems like England are the side under pressure now. Join us in a while for the final session.

After more than 160 overs, England have finally managed to wrap up the Indian innings to get a lead of 49. Centuries from Pujara and Vijay set things up yesterday for the hosts although the tourists did turn things around a bit by reducing India from 318/2 to 361/6. Kohli got a start but got out in weird circumstances as the visitors looked like taking control of the match. However, Ashwin's brilliant fifty led a lower order fightback to cut down England's lead drastically.

The visitors started the first hour well with the big wickets of Rahane and Kohli, the latter being a bit unfortunate as he got out hit wicket. The score read 361/6 at the Indian captain's dismissal and England were sensing an opportunity to run through the lower order. However, Saha and Ashwin have stitched a useful unbroken half century stand to keep the tourists at bay.

Length ball wider outside off, no stroke offered to that one.
Length around off, Kohli shuffles and tucks it towards short mid-wicket.
Length ball outside off, blocked well by Kohli to the off side.
England aren't happy with the shape of the ball. Dharmasena has a look with the 8-shape gauge and signals for a replacement.
Full and outside off, blocked off the front foot towards mid on.
Fuller around off, Rahane leans forward and blocks it out.
A bit streaky! Kohli gets an under edge on the pull that goes just past Bairstow towards fine leg. A single taken.
Kept outside off, Kohli gets on the front foot and defends.
Length ball outside off, Kohli leans into it and defends it out.
Length ball outside off, Kohli defends off the back foot.
Full and outside off, blocked off the front foot to the covers.
Dug in short on middle, doesn't rise much as Rahane swivels to pull it through mid-wicket. Didn't quite connect as well as he would have liked but will get a couple.
Dug in short around off, Rahane sways away from the bumper.
Full and outside off, Rahane gets forward to block.
Good length outside off, blocked firmly off the back foot.
Length ball outside off, Rahane flashes at it but is beaten.

That one gripped! Length ball angled in from well outside off, the ball moves away a bit off that dry crack. Rahane plays inside the line of it. Broad's been targeting the crack from yesterday onward.
Full and wide outside off, no stroke offered to that one.
Dug in short and Rahane responds with the pull towards long leg for a run.
Good length closer to off, Rahane blocks it firmly from the crease.
Length ball outside off, defended well off the front foot solidly.
Good length outside off, shaping away, no stroke offered to that one.
Very full and wide outside off, Rahane squeezes it to the covers.
CHRIS WOAKES from the other end.
FOUR! Signature Kohli stroke! Full ball outside off, he just leans into it and creams it through cover-point. Beautifully timed and the ball races away to the fence.
Good length closer to off, Kohli defends it well from the crease.
Short ball on middle, Rahane swivels to pull it through backward square leg for a single.
Another length ball wider outside off, no stroke offered to that one.
Length ball but too wide to make Rahane play at it.
Good length outside off, no shot offered to that one.
STUART BROAD to bowl from the other end.
Going down leg, Rahane clips it in front of square to get off the mark!
Similar delivery, defended well off the front foot to the off side.
Tossed up outside off, Rahane presses forward and defends to short cover.
We are ready to kick start the first session. The players and umpires walk out in the middle. KOHLI to continue his batting and RAHANE comes to the crease. ANSARI to continue his over. Here we go...

The ball is in the court of the visitors at the moment but the pitch hasn't shown much signs of breaking up. They need to make good use of the crease angles and rough patches to keep the batsmen on their toes. Will the Indian middle and lower middle order close in the gap or even take some sort of lead or will the tourists close the lid on the hosts and take a firm griphold? It promises to be an eventful day of Test cricket.

Hello and a warm welcome on Day 4 of the first Test between India and England in Rajkot. With Pujara and Vijay both departing in the final session yesterday after playing eye catching knocks, it has left the match delicately poised. A lot depends on the heroic pair of Kohli and Rahane to counter the English attack and weave together a substantial partnership. On the other hand, the English side would like to see the back of both soon.
... DAY 4, SESSION 1...

India's top order have done the hard work to give the hosts a strong foundation. However, the shaky finish will surely inspire England. The home side still trail by 218 runs although there is plenty of batting to come. The visitors will hope to nip out a couple early on tomorrow to put further pressure on the Indians. India will know that one more partnership will get them to safety. Should be another absorbing day. Join us at 0930 IST for the fourth day's play. Till then, it's good bye from us.

With the pitch hardly offering anything barring the odd turning ball and minimal reverse swing, England's bowlers were made to toil hard. Woakes was the standout bowler while Broad was tidy too. One area where England's bowlers succeeded was in keeping a check on the run flow particularly after lunch. Among the spinners, Rashid was probably the most threatening but was underbowled by Cook. The surprise was to see Ali being ineffective as the Indians took the attack to him.

Double strike just before stumps has given England some respite but it has still been India's day. The hosts were driven by majestic tons from Pujara and Vijay after the early loss of Gambhir. The 209-run stand put India's innings in cruise control mode before Pujara departed to a loose shot. With his skipper Kohli for company, it seemed like Vijay would bat through till stumps before a lapse of concentration saw the latter walk back to the pavilion. The nightwatchman Mishra didn't last long either as England managed to end the day on a high.

OUT! THE PLOY TO SEND THE NIGHTWATCHMAN DOES NOT WORK! Bowls it quicker around middle and off, comes in with the arm and bounces a bit more than the batsman expects. Mishra looks to negotiate it with the angle but gets an inside edge onto his pads and the ball lobs towards Haseeb again. He is alert out there and bends to his left to take a sharp catch in front of him. Good passage of play for the English side in the end and THAT WILL BE STUMPS ON DAY 3!
Mishra presses forward to the loopy delivery and blocks it into the ground.
A touch short outside off, spinning away. Kohli camps back and cuts it through point for a single. Exposes the night watchman at the fag end.
ZAFAR ANSARI comes back on.
The nightwatchman AMIT MISHRA walks out to bat.

OUT! THE MARATHON KNOCK FROM VIJAY COMES TO AN END! Slips in a googly on a length on off, spins back in. Vijay goes back and looks to nudge it through but only manages to glove it towards the youngster Haseeb at short leg. He shows good reflexes and grabs a good catch. Crucial breakthrough for the English side!
Tossed up delivery, Kohli drives it with the spin wide of mid off for a single.
Kohli presses forward and blocks it into the ground.
Bowls it from the front of his hand and it skids through on its line. Virat goes deep in his crease to block it out.
Outside off, spinning away. The Indian skipper lets it go.
On a length at the stumps, Kohli camps back and defends it to the off side.
ADIL RASHID comes back.
Full length ball on off, Vijay comes forward and defends it back to the bowler.

Fullish delivery around middle, Vijay drives it to Root at mid on. He has a shy at the bowler's end but misses. Vijay was in anyways. There is no one to back up and therefore concedes an overthrow in the process.
Good length ball outside off, shapes back in late after pitching. Kohli lets it go through.
Back of a length ball outside off, Kohli shuffles a bit and taps it towards cover-point.
Digs it in very short outside off, zips through the pitch. Virat ducks under it and lets it sail through the keeper.
On a length on off, Virat has it well covered and defends it to the off side.
Kohli clips it with the spin in between the gap at mid on and mid-wicket for a single.
Outside off, spins in this time. Kohli stays back and defends.
A touch short outside off, going away with the arm. Virat cuts it late down to third man. Couple taken!
Very full on middle, Virat whips it to mid-wicket but fails to find the gap.
Fullish delivery on middle and leg, pushed towards mid on with soft hands.
Pitches it around leg stump, Virat stays back and nudges it to backward square leg.
Follows it up with a quickish delivery on a length outside off, Vijay is not bothered to play at that one.
Slower off cutter outside off, at 119 clicks. Vijay makes a watchful leave.
Follows it up with a full length ball on off, looking to catch Vijay off guard. He is up to it as he defends it back to Woakes.
Good length delivery outside off, shapes away after pitching. Vijay is not going to flirt with those.
Back of a length ball outside off, Vijay points his bat skywards and leaves it alone.
On a length and straying on the hips, Vijay hangs back and tickles it down to fine leg for a couple.
Kohli brings his bottom hand in play and clips it to the fielder at mid-wicket.

Pitches it on leg stump, clipped to short mid-wicket.
Straying on the pads, nudged round the corner with ease for a single.
Tosses it up outside off, Vijay presses forward and defends past silly point.
Lands it around middle and leg, Kohli stays back and nudges it towards backward square leg for a single.
Outside off, left alone by Vijay.
Shortish delivery, Virat rises with the bounce and tucks it to backward square leg for a single.
On a length around off, bounces a bit extra. Virat gets on top of it and taps it to point.
Back of a length ball angling into middle and leg, Virat defends it to the leg side.
On a length that is a bit wide outside off, Kohli camps back and punches it to the covers.
Fullish ball outside off, Virat points his bat skywards and lets it sail through to the keeper.
CHRIS WOAKES comes back to bowl.
Back of a length on off, stays low. Vijay camps back but has to bend to block it to the leg side.
SIX! PURE CLASS! Loopy ball outside off, Vijay has his dancing shoes on and nails his lofted shot over the long off boundary with utmost ease.
Back of a length ball at the stumps, Kohli helps it with the turn in front of square for a single.

Kohli stays back and tucks it past the fielder at short leg. Vijay wants the single for some reason but it was not on. Goes back!
Tossed up outside off, Kohli looks to defend but misses and is rapped on the pads. Muted appeal for LBW turned down. The impact looked well outside off.
Back of a length on off, Kohli stays back and pushes it towards mid on.
FOUR! Dug in short angling towards leg stump, Virat walks across and gets a fine tickle on it and it just passes wide of the diving Bairstow to his left. Goes through to the fence.
Full length ball outside off, Kohli puts in a confident stride forward and defends it to short cover.

Shortish delivery, rising up on Virat. He is standing out of his crease and looks to clip it through but toe ends it down the pitch. Looks for a run and ends up rolling it back to Broad off his boot. He has shy and hits the stumps but Kohli was back in.

7th Test ton for Murali Vijay!

.....DAY 3, SESSION 3.....

England's bowlers were very disciplined with Broad being the standout with a very miserly spell. However, the tourists couldn't cause much trouble and had to be content by keeping a lid on the scoring rate. The odd ball has spun and there has been some reverse swing too but generally it's still remained a good batting pitch for those who are willing to apply themselves. England will hope to bottle down the runs and hope that India's batting implodes at some stage. Join us in a while for the final session.

This session - 29 overs, 66 runs, 0 wickets. Another solid session for the Indians. Vijay and Pujara continued to grind the English bowling to dust without any real trouble. The latter did get a reprieve as he used DRS to successfully overturn an lbw decision against him. Apart from that, he hardly put a foot wrong and is just a run short of his 9th Test ton. Vijay is eyeing a century of his own as well and has also looked very compact out there.

Loopy and full outside off, Vijay drives it with lazy elegance to mid off.

Shortish delivery outside off, Pujara rocks back and cuts it through point for a single.
Loopy ball on off, defended solidly down the track.
Back of a length ball, turning into Vijay. He raises his arms and takes it on the thigh pad.
Stays back to the length delivery and punches it to mid on.
FOUR! CRAFTY SHOT! Tossed it up on off, Vijay takes position for the reverse sweep and executes it perfectly through the fine leg region for a boundary.

Turning in from outside off, Vijay stays back and tucks it through square leg for a single.

Pujara stays back and defends.

A bit short outside off, slapped off the back foot through the covers for a single. Stokes' throw at the bowler's end finds no back up as it goes to deep mid-wicket. Another brace added. Sloppy from England.

Length ball outside off, pushed off the back foot to the covers.

Welcome back for the second session. India will hope that the current partnership flourishes further as they look to accomplish their primary goal of avoiding the follow-on before thinking of bigger things. England will know that a wicket can easily bring another due to the scoreboard pressure. It shall be CHRIS WOAKES to begin proceedings after lunch.
.....DAY 3, SESSION 2.....

There weren't many demons in the track although the surface is definitely showing signs of deteriorating at some stage. England's bowlers tried hard and Broad's first ball strike was the perfect tonic they needed to begin the day. However, since then, they have been countered by some really smart batting. Only Woakes was probing in his spell while Rashid's last over before the break was brilliant too. He will bowl a lot after lunch for sure. Join us in a while for the second session.

A very good session for India despite losing Gambhir off the second over of the day. Pujara and Vijay have stitched a brilliant unbroken 94-run partnership to thwart the English bowling attack. The former has been very busy out there, looking very fluent barring a spell from Woakes where he was hit on the helmet thrice. Vijay has been his usual rock solid self although he did have to survive a tough last over before lunch.
Flighted ball around off, Vijay goes back and plays it towards backward point. THAT'S LUNCH ON DAY 3!
Tossed up outside off, defended towards point.
Leg spinner on off, turning away with extra bounce. Vijay prods forward to defend but is beaten.

LOUD SHOUT APPEAL FOR LBW TURNED DOWN! Good decision to not take the review! Slips in a googly outside off, turning back in. Vijay prods forward to defend but plays down the wrong line and misses. The umpire thinks about the appeal but turns it down. Looked really close to the naked eye! Nasser Hussain on air mentions that, "Vijay was well forward and it hit him above the knee roll." The replays show that it would have gone over the stumps. Good call by Cook and Bairstow to not take the review! So Nasser was spot on there!

Tossed up on off, driven to Stokes at covers who dives to make a half-stop. No runs conceded.

On the pads, Vijay nudges it through backward square leg for a single.
Good length ball outside off, swings away late after pitching. Vijay shoulders his arms to let that through.

Fullish ball well outside off, Pujara comes forward and leaves it alone.
Slips in a googly again outside off, Vijay comes forward and defends it.
Loopy ball around off, spinning away. Defended towards point.
Tossed up around off, Pujara drives it towards Stokes at mid off who fumbles and concedes a single. Rashid is not pleases.

Low full toss on off, Murali makes room and eases it to long off for a single.

FOUR! EASY PICKINGS! Straying on the pads, Pujara clips it round the corner nicely. The ball races to the fence! 8 runs off the over!

Fullish delivery outside off, luring him into a free flowing drive. He resists the temptation!

Comes forward and defends it to the off side.

In between full and good length and at the stumps, Murali leans ahead and defends it down the track.
Fuller length ball outside off, Vijay defends it towards cover-point.
Fullish ball on middle and leg, Pujara clips it to wide of mid on and gets across for a quick single.
FOUR! PURE TIMING! Full length ball outside off, Pujara strides foward and drives it to perfection through extra cover. The placement was so precise on that one!
Full length outswinger wide outside off, but its too wide to make Che play.

The players and umpires are making their way out to the middle. Can the Indian openers build further and give the hosts a big platform or will the English bowlers make inroads? Let's find out. It shall be MOEEN ALI to begin proceedings on day three.

It is rare that we see India on the back foot in a Test match at home. The English side have an opportunity to put the shackles on the hosts by employing aggressive field positions. While, it will be a test of character and temperament for the hosts, let's see whether they are able to steer the ship to safe harbours.

Hello and a warm welcome on Day 3 of the first Test between India and England in Rajkot. The strong Indian batting would know that they have an uphill task in front of them. Though the pitch does not have any demons in it but the odd ball is playing tricks. The cracks have started to widen up. The visitors have the cushion of 3 spinners as well.
... DAY 3, SESSION 1...

The pitch still looks good to bat on and India will like to make good use of it. Although the ball has started to turn a lot now so the hosts need to be careful as England have three spinners. That ends a riveting day of Test cricket! India did well not to lose any wickets before stumps after England posted 537. Both the openers negotiated the English bowlers well and went back to the dressing room unscathed. Earlier in the day, Ben Stokes and Moeen Ali's fine tons and Bairstow's attacking knock helped England post a massive first innings total. The Indian bowlers were made to toil hard after a long time at home.
